how_to_apply: Visit the official recruitment portal at npcrecruitments.in.
Read Advertisement No. NPC/TA/1/2026 carefully.
Check the essential qualification, five-year experience requirement and age conditions.
Click the online registration option.
Enter your name, date of birth and gender exactly as recorded in the Class 10 certificate.
Provide a valid email address and mobile number.
Complete OTP verification and receive the registration credentials.
Log in using the registration number and password.
Enter your personal information and reservation category.
Select Technical Assistant (Accounts), Technical Assistant or both posts.
If applying for both posts, select the first-preference post.
Enter educational qualifications and marks.
Provide details of desirable qualifications, where applicable.
Enter each period of employment separately, including employer, designation, dates and duties.
Select the applicable age-relaxation category, if eligible.
Choose a Phase-I examination centre.
Enter PwBD and scribe-related information, where applicable.
Upload the required photograph, signature, qualification certificates and experience documents.
Review the complete application.
Pay the prescribed application fee, if applicable.
Accept the declaration and click Final Submit.
Complete submission before 28 December 2026 at 5:00 PM.
Download and preserve the final submitted application PDF.
Important: NPC will not provide an application correction window after Final Submit. Candidates should carefully check all details before completing final submission.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: The National Productivity Council has announced the application schedule and tentative examination dates for Technical Assistant and Technical Assistant (Accounts) recruitment. Important: The online registration and fee payment facility closes at 5:00 PM on 28 December 2026. Examination dates are tentative and may be revised through the official NPC recruitment portal.

content_sections.heading: NPC Vacancy 2026 - 15 Technical Assistant Posts
content_sections.text: NPC has announced 15 Group B vacancies across two positions. The category-wise vacancy distribution is provided below. One vacancy in each post is earmarked for eligible Persons with Benchmark Disabilities having Locomotor Disability involving One Arm (OA) or One Leg (OL). Reservation Clarification: The two PwBD vacancies are included in the total of 15 and are not additional posts. PwBD candidates from eligible categories can apply against these earmarked vacancies and will be adjusted according to their applicable category. There is no reserved ST vacancy for either post. Technical Assistant also has no SC or EWS reserved vacancy. Candidates belonging to categories without a reserved vacancy may compete for unreserved positions without reserved-category age relaxation.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF
content_sections.text: National Productivity Council has published the detailed for recruitment of Technical Assistant (Accounts) and Technical Assistant posts. The notification includes vacancies, qualifications, experience requirements, age relaxation, application fees, the examination pattern, subject-wise syllabus, document specifications and selection rules. Official NPC Career Notifications: NPC Career Notification Page

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Only Indian nationals possessing the prescribed qualification and relevant professional experience are eligible to apply. Candidates must possess a recognized Degree in Commerce and at least five years of relevant experience in accounts, finance, auditing, taxation or budget-related work. The experience must have been gained in Central Government, State Government, a Public Sector Undertaking or an autonomous organization. A postgraduate qualification in Commerce or passing the Intermediate Examination conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India or the Institute of Cost Accountants of India is desirable but not mandatory. Applicants must possess a recognized Bachelor's Degree in Arts, Science, Commerce or Management, along with five years of experience in administrative or office-related work. Relevant experience includes noting and drafting, establishment work, procurement, record management and file administration in an eligible Government, PSU or autonomous organization. A postgraduate degree in any discipline is considered desirable. Yes. Candidates holding a recognized B.Com. degree may apply for both posts if they separately satisfy the relevant five-year experience requirements. Yes. Candidates holding recognized Arts or Science degrees can apply for Technical Assistant positions, provided they have the required administrative or office work experience. BA or B.Sc. qualifications alone do not meet the essential degree requirement for Technical Assistant (Accounts). No. Both posts require five years of relevant full-time paid experience after acquiring the essential qualification. Internships, articleships, apprenticeships, part-time work and honorary service are not counted as qualifying experience. The notification specifically requires qualifying experience in Central/State Government, a Public Sector Undertaking or an autonomous body. Experience solely in ordinary private-sector employment does not satisfy the stated essential experience condition.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Age Limit
content_sections.text: The general maximum age limit for both positions is 30 years as on 28 December 2026 . For the unrelaxed age limit, candidates must have been born on or after 29 December 1996. Important: SC and OBC age relaxations are available only against the relevant reserved vacancies. The Technical Assistant post has no SC reserved vacancy, so SC applicants competing for unreserved vacancies cannot claim the SC age relaxation. Age relaxations are generally not cumulative, except for the expressly permitted PwBD relaxation combined with applicable OBC-NCL or SC relaxation. One qualifying year of service is counted when the candidate worked directly for NPC for at least 180 days in that year. A maximum of five qualifying years can be counted. Service through outsourcing agencies, manpower suppliers, internships or apprenticeships is excluded. Candidates claiming this relaxation must upload the prescribed service certificate issued by the Head of the concerned NPC office.

content_sections.text: The application fee depends on the candidate's category, gender and number of posts selected. Payment Mode: Debit Card, Credit Card or Internet Banking through the official recruitment portal. Any additional bank transaction charges are payable by the applicant. The examination fee is non-refundable.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Selection Process
content_sections.text: The National Productivity Council will select candidates through a two-phase examination system and subsequent verification. Online application submission and fee payment, where applicable. Phase-I Computer-Based Preliminary Examination. Shortlisting for Phase-II in the prescribed ratio. Phase-II Descriptive Examination. Digital Competency IT Practical Test. Preparation of post-wise merit lists. Original document verification. Medical fitness and character verification. Final appointment. Important: NPC explicitly states that there will be no interview .

content_sections.heading: NPC Technical Assistant Exam Pattern 2027
content_sections.text: The examination comprises a Preliminary MCQ paper and Phase-II assessments. The examination medium is English. The Phase-I examination is a screening test. Its marks will be used for shortlisting candidates for Phase-II and for tie-breaking where applicable, but will not be included in the final merit calculation. Candidates will be shortlisted for Phase-II in a 1:12 ratio , subject to the prescribed category-wise rules and tie conditions. All candidates obtaining the same marks as the last shortlisted candidate will also be shortlisted.

rows.subject: Numerical Ability, Data Interpretation and Basic Computer Knowledge

content_sections.heading: NPC Phase-II Main Examination Pattern 2027
content_sections.text: The Phase-II Main Examination includes a Descriptive Examination and a qualifying Digital Competency Test. The descriptive examination will be conducted in pen-and-paper mode. Separate papers will be held for Technical Assistant (Accounts) and Technical Assistant. The examination will assess post-specific professional knowledge, office or financial procedures, communication skills and the ability to prepare notes, drafts and written answers. The marks obtained in the descriptive examination will form the basis of final merit for candidates who qualify in the IT Practical Test. The Digital Competency Test is common to both posts and will assess practical computer skills using MS Office 2019 or later. Important: Candidates must secure the minimum qualifying marks separately in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Obtaining 50 marks in total is not sufficient if the candidate fails to meet the minimum required score in any individual software package. Candidates shortlisted for both posts will take the common Digital Competency Test only once, but must appear separately for both descriptive papers.

content_sections.heading: NPC Technical Assistant Syllabus 2027
content_sections.text: The official notification includes a detailed syllabus for the preliminary examination, domain knowledge and Digital Competency Test. Current affairs and important events. Indian history and culture. Indian geography. Economic developments. General policy and governance. Scientific research. India and neighbouring countries. Verbal and non-verbal reasoning. Semantic and numerical analogies. Number and figure series. Classification and Venn diagrams. Space orientation. Logical and critical thinking. Problem-solving and decision-making. Pattern folding and figure completion. Word building and analytical reasoning. Number systems, decimals and fractions. Percentage and ratio. Average, profit and loss. Simple and compound interest. Time and work. Time, speed and distance. Partnership and mixture calculations. Tables, graphs and data interpretation. Computer fundamentals. CPU, memory and input/output devices. Microsoft Office basics. Spotting errors. Fill in the blanks. Synonyms and antonyms. Idioms and phrases. One-word substitution. Sentence improvement. Active and passive voice. Direct and indirect speech. Sentence rearrangement. Cloze test and reading comprehension.

content_sections.heading: NPC Technical Assistant Domain Syllabus
content_sections.text: The Technical Assistant domain examination focuses on office administration, Government procedures and relevant service rules. Note preparation and drafting. Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure (CSMOP). Fundamental Rules and Supplementary Rules. Central Civil Services Leave Rules, 1972. CCS Conduct Rules, 1964. CCS Classification, Control and Appeal Rules, 1965. General Financial Rules, 2017. General Provident Fund Rules. Government grievance handling through CPGRAMS. Government e-Marketplace (GeM). Right to Information Act, 2005.

content_sections.heading: NPC Technical Assistant Accounts Syllabus
content_sections.text: The Technical Assistant (Accounts) examination focuses on financial and cost accounting, taxation, auditing and business laws. Accounting concepts and standards. Preparation of final accounts. Depreciation and inventory valuation. Cash flow statements. Revenue recognition. Property, plant and equipment. Government grants. Foreign exchange transactions. Accounting for share capital. Cost concepts and classifications. Cost accounting systems. Job and process costing. Activity-based costing. Cost-volume-profit analysis. Budgeting and standard costing. Variance analysis. Cost control and reduction. Responsibility accounting. Income Tax concepts and computation. Heads of income and deductions. Set-off and carry-forward of losses. Tax Deducted at Source. Goods and Services Tax fundamentals. Company audit and tax audit. Indian Contract Act, 1872. Companies Act, 2013. Information Technology Act, 2000.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Final Merit List
content_sections.text: The final merit list will be prepared separately for the two posts. Only candidates who qualify in the Digital Competency Test will be considered for final merit ranking based on their Phase-II Descriptive Examination marks. If two candidates obtain equal marks, preference will be determined in the following order: Possession of a desirable qualification. Higher marks in the Phase-I examination for the relevant post. Older age. Candidates who qualify for both posts will be considered according to the first-preference post indicated in their application and the applicable merit and selection rules. NPC may maintain a reserve list valid for one year from the date of declaration of the result.

content_sections.text: Eligible candidates must submit their applications through the official NPC recruitment portal. Apply Online: https://npcrecruitments.in/ Application Start: 28 November 2026 at 10:00 AM. Application Last Date: 28 December 2026 at 5:00 PM. Candidates may apply for one or both posts using a single application. Those selecting both posts must indicate their first-preference position.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Reservation and Certificates
content_sections.text: NPC will implement reservation according to the Government of India rules specified in the notification. OBC-NCL candidates must have their caste listed in the Central OBC List and possess the prescribed Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued on or before the closing date. EWS candidates must submit a valid Income and Asset Certificate for FY 2026-27 based on income for FY 2025-26. Eligible PwBD candidates must possess the prescribed certificate or UDID card showing at least 40% disability involving One Arm or One Leg. Applicants claiming reservation or age relaxation must ensure their certificates satisfy the Central Government recruitment requirements.

content_sections.heading: NPC Recruitment 2026 Probation, Posting and Training
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will be appointed under the terms prescribed by the National Productivity Council. Final appointment will be subject to document verification, medical fitness and character and antecedent verification.

faq.question: Q1. What is the organization conducting this recruitment?
faq.answer: The recruitment is conducted by the National Productivity Council (NPC) for filling up Technical Assistant and Technical Assistant (Accounts) positions across various offices in India.

faq.question: Q2. How many total vacancies are announced under NPC Advt No NPC/TA/1/2026?
faq.answer: A total of 15 vacancies have been announced, which includes 10 posts for Technical Assistant (Accounts) and 5 posts for Technical Assistant.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to submit the online application?
faq.answer: The last date to submit the online application and complete the fee payment is 28 December 2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification required for Technical Assistant (Accounts)?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Degree in Commerce along with 5 years of relevant experience in accounts, finance, audit, taxation, or budget work.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary structure for these posts?
faq.answer: Selected candidates will receive a salary under Pay Level-6 of the 7th CPC Pay Matrix, ranging from Rs. 35,400 to Rs. 1,12,400 per month.

faq.question: Q6. Is there any application fee for female or reserved category candidates?
faq.answer: Yes, women candidates of all categories, as well as SC, ST, and PwBD candidates, are completely exempted from paying the application fee.

faq.question: Q7. What is the maximum age limit to apply?
faq.answer: The maximum age limit is 30 years as on the closing date of application, with applicable relaxations for reserved categories as per government rules.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for NPC Technical Assistant posts?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises Phase-I Preliminary Examination, Phase-II Descriptive Examination, and a Common Digital Competency (IT Practical) Test followed by document verification.

faq.question: Q9. When is the Phase-I examination scheduled to be held?
faq.answer: The Phase-I computer-based preliminary examination is scheduled to be conducted on 24 January 2027.

faq.question: Q10. Where can candidates apply online for this recruitment?
faq.answer: Eligible candidates can apply online through the official recruitment portal provided by the National Productivity Council at https://npcrecruitments.in.
